meaning:
ἀπ-εκ-δύω
to strip off clothes or arms; mid., to strip off from oneself: Col.3:9; to strip, despoil (mid, for act., ICC, in l; but cf. Lft., Ellic.), Col.2:15.†
(AS)

renderings.kjv: seeing that ye have put off

elsewhere.note: Having stripped the principalities and the powers, he made a show of them openly, triumphing over them in it.
